concepts.name: Enterprise App Catalogue
concepts.explanation: A curated repository within Intune that simplifies the discovery, deployment, and automatic updating of common third-party Win32 applications.
concepts.example: Deploying Google Chrome or Adobe Acrobat Reader directly from the built-in catalog without manually packaging the installation files.
concepts.default_value: App updates are set to 'Show all visual notifications' to the user by default, and update checks run automatically in the background.

concepts.name: Company Portal App
concepts.explanation: The user-facing storefront application where employees can self-install authorized apps, view device compliance status, and contact IT support.
concepts.example: A marketing employee opening the app to download an approved copy of Camtasia labeled as 'Available'.
concepts.default_value: Syncs automatically with Intune every 8 hours on Windows devices.

concepts.name: App configuration policies
concepts.explanation: Instructions pushed to managed applications to pre-configure settings, accounts, or branding before the user opens the app.
concepts.example: Pre-populating the corporate server URL in the Zoom app so users do not have to type it.
concepts.default_value: Configured using Configuration designer (UI format) or raw JSON data.

concepts.name: App settings
concepts.explanation: The individual, granular configuration values or key-pair keys defined within an app configuration policy to customize application behavior.
concepts.example: Setting the key 'com.microsoft.outlook.EmailProfile.AccountDomain' to your company's domain.
concepts.default_value: No default keys are populated; settings are completely dependent on the specific app developer’s documentation.

concepts.name: Application assignments
concepts.explanation: The process of targeting applications to specific users or devices as 'Required', 'Available', or 'Uninstall'.
concepts.example: Assigning Microsoft Teams as 'Required' for all employees, ensuring it installs automatically.
concepts.default_value: Delivery optimization priority is set to 'Background' for Required apps, and app availability is set to 'As soon as possible'.

concepts.name: Application information
concepts.explanation: The metadata of an app—such as name, description, publisher, and icon—displayed to users within the Company Portal.
concepts.example: Uploading a high-resolution Slack logo and a 2-sentence description so users know exactly what they are installing.
concepts.default_value: 'Show this as a featured app in the Company Portal' is toggled to No by default.

concepts.name: Managed Google Play App
concepts.explanation: Android applications sourced from the secure enterprise Google Play store and approved by IT for deployment to Android Enterprise devices.
concepts.example: Approving the OneDrive app in the Google Play console so it instantly appears in your Intune app inventory.
concepts.default_value: App runtime permissions are set to 'Prompt' user consent by default.

concepts.name: Line of business app
concepts.explanation: A custom, in-house developed application (such as an .msi, .apk, or .ipa) uploaded directly to Intune for deployment.
concepts.example: Uploading a custom-built inventory-tracking .msi app developed by your internal software team.
concepts.default_value: 'Ignore app version' is set to No (meaning Intune will strictly check the app version during evaluation).

concepts.name: Mobile application management (MAM)
concepts.explanation: A management approach focused strictly on securing and controlling corporate data within applications without requiring the user to enroll their entire personal device.
concepts.example: Securing business emails by applying corporate restrictions exclusively to the Outlook mobile app on an employee's personal iPhone (BYOD).
concepts.default_value: Data protection applies immediately to any application natively integrated with the Microsoft Intune App SDK.

concepts.name: Android Enterprise system app
concepts.explanation: Pre-installed, native device applications (like the camera or calculator) that IT can explicitly enable or disable on corporate Android devices.
concepts.example: Unhiding the native Samsung Camera app on a dedicated corporate barcode-scanning device.
concepts.default_value: Native system apps are automatically hidden/disabled on Android Enterprise fully managed profiles to ensure a clean slate.

concepts.name: Difference assignments all devices, users, or single group
concepts.explanation: Targeting 'All Devices' applies settings regardless of who logs in, 'All Users' ensures settings follow the person across devices, while a 'Single Group' confines the policy to a specific, scoped subset of identities.
concepts.example: Assigning a VPN profile to All Devices (so it is ready at the login screen) vs. assigning an expense app to a Single Group named 'Finance-Dept'.
concepts.default_value: Intune defaults to evaluating Exclusion groups first, overriding any Inclusion groups.

concepts.name: Add android store apps
concepts.explanation: The process of adding publicly available applications from the Managed Google Play store into the Intune console for deployment.
concepts.example: Searching for and adding the Salesforce mobile app from the integrated Play Store tab.
concepts.default_value: The application syncs into your main Intune console roughly 10 to 15 minutes after approval.

concepts.name: Microsoft 365 apps with intune
concepts.explanation: A built-in Intune app suite category that allows administrators to easily configure and deploy the Microsoft 365 productivity suite to Windows or macOS endpoints.
concepts.example: Deploying Excel, Word, and PowerPoint to a fleet of new laptops in a single click.
concepts.default_value: Update channel defaults to 'Current Channel', and old architecture versions default to '64-bit'.

concepts.name: App protection policy
concepts.explanation: A set of security rules (like restricting copy-paste or requiring an app PIN) that safeguards corporate data inside specific apps, regardless of whether the device is enrolled.
concepts.example: Restricting an employee from copying text out of corporate Outlook and pasting it into personal WhatsApp.
concepts.default_value: 'Target to apps on all device types' is set to Yes (covering both managed and unmanaged personal devices).

concepts.name: Policy for office apps
concepts.explanation: Targeted app protection or configuration rules applied specifically to core Microsoft productivity applications like Word, Excel, and Outlook to protect corporate data.
concepts.example: Blocking users from saving corporate Excel spreadsheets directly to a personal Dropbox account.
concepts.default_value: Handled via the Microsoft 365 Apps security baseline which auto-configures common macro-blocking behaviors.

concepts.name: Data Protection
concepts.explanation: The section of an app protection policy that controls data movement, such as blocking 'Save As' to personal storage or preventing screenshots.
concepts.example: Setting corporate files to automatically save only to OneDrive for Business.
concepts.default_value: 'Backup org data to Android/iOS cloud backups' is set to Block.

concepts.name: Access Requirements
concepts.explanation: The security criteria inside an app protection policy that a user must meet to open an app, such as setting a complex PIN or providing biometric authentication.
concepts.example: Requiring a 4-digit PIN and FaceID to unlock the corporate Outlook app.
concepts.default_value: PIN type is Numeric, minimum length is 4 digits, and biometric override is Allowed.

concepts.name: Conditional Launch
concepts.explanation: A mechanism that checks device health and user compliance at app startup, blocking access or wiping data if conditions (like a minimum OS version) aren't met.
concepts.example: Prompting a user that they cannot open their work email because their iPhone is running an outdated iOS version.
concepts.default_value: Max PIN attempts before a local data wipe is set to 5 attempts.

concepts.name: Device Rooted or jailbroken
concepts.explanation: A critical health check that identifies devices where operating system security restrictions have been bypassed, making them unsafe to access corporate data.
concepts.example: Instantly blocking access to corporate OneDrive the moment a user jailbreaks their iPhone using tools like checkra1n.
concepts.default_value: The default action configured for rooted/jailbroken devices is Block Access (can be configured to Wipe Data).

concepts.name: Organization data encryption
concepts.explanation: The mandatory, software-level encryption applied by Intune app protection policies to isolate and secure corporate data stored within managed apps on mobile devices.
concepts.example: Automatically encrypting data caches stored inside the local storage sandbox of the Microsoft Teams mobile app.
concepts.default_value: 'Encrypt org data' is set to Require in all standard MAM policies.

concepts.name: Wipe data
concepts.explanation: A targeted remote action that selectively deletes only corporate data from protected applications, leaving the user's personal photos and files untouched.
concepts.example: Offboarding a contractor and wiping corporate emails off their personal iPad without deleting their personal photos.
concepts.default_value: Once initiated, the wipe command executes the very next time the targeted application connects to the internet.

concepts.name: MAM vs. MDM conflicts
concepts.explanation: A scenario where Mobile Application Management and Mobile Device Management policies overlap, typically resolved because Intune automatically defers to the more restrictive data protection rule.
concepts.example: An MDM policy allows copy-paste across the whole phone, but a MAM app protection policy blocks it inside Outlook; the MAM policy wins for Outlook data.
concepts.default_value: When identity-based MAM and device-based MDM policies conflict, MAM (App Protection) policies take precedence regarding data handling within that app.

concepts.name: Device Configuration Settings Catalogue
concepts.explanation: A comprehensive, searchable interface in Intune containing all individual settings available for customization across various device platforms.
concepts.example: Searching for 'Bluetooth' to quickly find and disable the setting that allows corporate laptops to discover unknown devices.
concepts.default_value: Settings are in a 'Not Configured' state until explicitly added to a profile by an administrator.

concepts.name: Device Configuration Templates
concepts.explanation: Pre-packaged logical groupings of settings tailored for specific scenarios (like VPN, Wi-Fi, or Certificates) to streamline policy creation.
concepts.example: Selecting the Wi-Fi template to push out your corporate network SSID and WPA2 security key to all laptops.
concepts.default_value: Templates come with standard enterprise baselines pre-selected, but require administrators to input environment-specific fields (like server names).

concepts.name: Device Configuration profile and Delivery Optimization
concepts.explanation: A configuration policy used to manage how Windows updates are downloaded, allowing devices to share update files locally to save internet bandwidth.
concepts.example: Configuring a branch office of 100 computers so only 1 machine downloads a major Windows update from the internet, while the other 99 pull it from that local machine.
concepts.default_value: Download mode defaults to 'HTTP blended with peering behind same NAT' (LAN peering enabled).

concepts.name: Delivery Optimization Template
concepts.explanation: A specific, pre-built settings template used to configure peer-to-peer caching behaviors for Windows updates.
concepts.example: Pushing out a configuration that limits Delivery Optimization caching to machines with at least 4GB of RAM and 32GB of free disk space.
concepts.default_value: Cache age limit is set to 7 days and the minimum file size allowed to cache is 50 MB.

concepts.name: Import administrative template
concepts.explanation: The ability to upload custom third-party group policy settings into Intune to manage applications or features not natively included in the console.
concepts.example: Uploading custom Google Chrome policies into Intune so you can enforce a corporate home page across Chrome users.
concepts.default_value: Requires matching pairs of custom structural files to be uploaded successfully before configuration can begin.

concepts.name: ADMX and ADML
concepts.explanation: The underlying XML-based files where .admx defines the structure of configuration settings and .adml provides the localized language text for those settings.
concepts.example: Uploading GoogleChrome.admx for system logic along with GoogleChrome.adml so the text labels show up in English inside the Intune portal.
concepts.default_value: Intune natively includes standard Windows OS ADMX files automatically updated by Microsoft.

concepts.name: Assignment filters for apps, policies, profiles
concepts.explanation: High-performance rules applied to policy assignments that dynamically include or exclude devices based on specific attributes like model, manufacturer, or OS version.
concepts.example: Creating a filter where 'device.model -startsWith "Surface Pro"' to ensure a specific hardware driver is only assigned to Microsoft Surface tablets.
concepts.default_value: Devices that do not match the evaluation rule are immediately skipped from processing during the policy evaluation cycle.

concepts.name: Group Policy Analytics
concepts.explanation: An assessment tool that analyzes imported on-premises Group Policy Objects (GPOs) to determine their compatibility and readiness for transition to cloud-based Intune policies.
concepts.example: Uploading an old corporate desktop GPO XML report and discovering that 85% of its settings have direct, modern equivalents in the Intune Settings Catalog.
concepts.default_value: Analysis reports map imported settings into three clear status labels: Supported, Not Supported, or Unknown.

concepts.name: Automatic Enrollment
concepts.explanation: A feature that seamlessly and automatically registers a device into Intune MDM as soon as it is joined to Microsoft Entra ID.
concepts.example: A user logging into their new Windows laptop with their corporate email for the first time, causing the machine to silently enroll into Intune management.
concepts.default_value: MDM User scope defaults to None until switched to All or Some to enable automatic enrollment.

concepts.name: Intune joined vs entra joined device
concepts.explanation: An Entra Joined device is registered with the cloud identity directory for authentication, whereas an Intune Joined device is explicitly enrolled in the management service to receive security policies and apps.
concepts.example: A laptop that can log in with cloud credentials is Entra Joined, but it won't receive configuration profiles until it undergoes MDM enrollment to become Intune Joined.
concepts.default_value: Modern Autopilot deployments configure devices to become both Entra Joined and Intune Managed simultaneously.

concepts.name: Apple Business Manager
concepts.explanation: A web-based portal by Apple that integrates with Intune to automate corporate-owned iOS, iPadOS, and macOS device deployment and management.
concepts.example: Purchasing 50 corporate iPhones from an authorized reseller and having their unique serial numbers automatically sync to your Intune environment.
concepts.default_value: Requires an active Apple ID configured with Two-Factor Authentication and an annual token renewal.

concepts.name: Android Enterprise
concepts.explanation: Google’s modern management framework for Android devices, offering secure corporate deployment models like Work Profile and Fully Managed.
concepts.example: Provisioning a corporate phone as Fully Managed so the IT department controls the entire device, preventing the installation of personal apps.
concepts.default_value: Enrolling via a standard QR code creates a 'Personally-owned device with a work profile' unless designated otherwise.

concepts.name: Device Limit Restrictions to User
concepts.explanation: An administrative policy that defines the maximum number of devices (up to 15) a single user is allowed to enroll into Intune.
concepts.example: Restricting an average office worker so they can only enroll a maximum of 3 personal devices into the system.
concepts.default_value: Out of the box, Intune sets the global device limit restriction to 15 devices per user.

concepts.name: Device Enrollment Manager (DEM)
concepts.explanation: A special administrative account status that allows a single user to enroll and manage up to 1,000 corporate devices instead of the standard user limit.
concepts.example: A staging technician using a single service account to enroll 300 shared retail tablets before sending them out to store branches.
concepts.default_value: No accounts are configured as DEM by default; they must be manually designated under the Enrollment portal.

concepts.name: Device Enrollment Manager Accounts
concepts.explanation: The specific user accounts designated with DEM permissions to facilitate large-scale, shared-device deployments.
concepts.example: Creating a non-expiring cloud account named 'it-staging-dem@yourcompany.com' to handle bulk hardware deployments.
concepts.default_value: An Intune tenant allows a maximum limit of 150 DEM accounts.

concepts.name: MDM server Apple Business Manager and Uploading Server token in intune
concepts.explanation: The secure handshake process where a public/private key token is exchanged to link Intune with Apple Business Manager for automated enrollments.
concepts.example: Downloading an encryption key from Intune, uploading it to Apple's deployment portal, and downloading the server token to finalize the secure pipeline.
concepts.default_value: The uploaded Apple Server Token (.p7m file) is valid for exactly 1 year and must be manually renewed annually.

concepts.name: Apple Automatic Device Enrollment (ADE)
concepts.explanation: A zero-touch enrollment method that forces Apple devices to automatically configure and enroll into Intune immediately upon initial power-on.
concepts.example: Unboxing a brand new factory iPad, turning it on, and seeing a custom screen that says 'Your Organization will automatically configure this iPad' before reaching the home page.
concepts.default_value: Setup Assistant screens like Apple Pay, Touch ID, and Siri are set to Show unless explicitly toggled to Hide in the Intune profile.

concepts.name: Automatic MDM Enrollment
concepts.explanation: A broader term for configuring an identity provider (like Entra ID) to automatically hand off device management to Intune without user intervention during setup.
concepts.example: Setting up a corporate policy so that any user connecting a personal Windows PC to their work account forces an automatic MDM check-in.
concepts.default_value: URLs for terms of use, discovery, and compliance are pre-populated with standard Microsoft cloud endpoints.

concepts.name: Device Enrollment restrictions
concepts.explanation: Global rules that block or allow specific device platforms, operating system versions, or personally owned (BYOD) devices from enrolling in Intune.
concepts.example: Creating an enrollment restriction rule that blocks all personal Android devices from enrolling, while allowing corporate ones.
concepts.default_value: The out-of-the-box system policy Allows all platforms (Windows, iOS, Android, macOS) for both Corporate and Personally-Owned enrollments.

concepts.name: Enrollment Status Page (ESP)
concepts.explanation: A visual screen displayed to users during initial device setup that tracks the progress of mandatory applications, certificates, and profiles being installed.
concepts.example: A new employee waiting during setup while a progress bar blocks access to the desktop until corporate security software is installed.
concepts.default_value: The default enrollment timeout before showing an error is set to 60 minutes.

concepts.name: Entra Join new windows device during OOBE
concepts.explanation: The process of a user typing their corporate credentials during the initial Windows Out-of-Box Experience to instantly register the machine in Microsoft Entra ID.
concepts.example: An employee opens a factory-sealed laptop, connects it to home Wi-Fi, types 'user@company.com', and the machine instantly joins the corporate identity directory.
concepts.default_value: The joining user is automatically designated as a Standard User on the local operating system configuration.

concepts.name: Configure Microsoft Entra connect Sync to Synchronize device objects
concepts.explanation: Setting up the on-premises sync tool to copy active directory computer accounts to the cloud to support hybrid deployment scenarios.
concepts.example: Syncing your legacy on-premises Windows 10 desktop computer objects into Azure AD so they can be recognized for Hybrid Entra Join configurations.
concepts.default_value: The synchronization delta engine runs automatically every 30 minutes by default.

concepts.name: Enable device Writeback in Microsoft Entra connect Sync
concepts.explanation: An advanced configuration that syncs cloud-registered device objects back to an on-premises Active Directory to support conditional access features.
concepts.example: Writing an Entra-registered iOS device identity back to your local Active Directory domain so on-premises applications can verify its identity.
concepts.default_value: This feature is Disabled by default and requires running the Entra Connect configuration wizard with domain admin rights to enable.

concepts.name: OS SKU
concepts.explanation: The specific edition of an operating system (such as Windows Home, Pro, or Enterprise) that dictates which features and Intune management capabilities are available.
concepts.example: Moving a device from Windows Pro to Windows Enterprise via an Intune license push to unlock advanced BitLocker key rotation.
concepts.default_value: Intune management capabilities are designed to target standard business-grade SKUs (Windows Pro/Enterprise) and explicitly exclude Windows Home edition.

concepts.name: OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer)
concepts.explanation: Hardware manufacturers (like Dell, HP, or Lenovo) that can pre-register device hardware hashes directly into an organization's Autopilot service.
concepts.example: Placing an order with Lenovo for 100 laptops and having them populate your Autopilot deployment list before the physical boxes even arrive.
concepts.default_value: Hardware registrations remain indefinitely in your tenant until the device is explicitly deleted by an administrator.

concepts.name: Windows Autopilot deployment profiles
concepts.explanation: Configuration files that define the exact user experience during Windows setup, specifying whether a device is user-driven, self-deploying, and if it hides privacy settings.
concepts.example: Configuring a profile so users don't see the Microsoft Software License Agreement (EULA) or privacy diagnostics toggles during setup.
concepts.default_value: Deployment mode defaults to User-driven, and Join type defaults to Microsoft Entra joined.

concepts.name: Autopilot Profiles
concepts.explanation: The distinct templates containing deployment rules assigned to hardware hashes to govern how a Windows machine installs its corporate image.
concepts.example: Creating a 'Kiosk-Profile' for shared front-desk machines vs. a 'Standard-User-Profile' for corporate employees.
concepts.default_value: New profiles default to making the primary enrolling user a standard Standard User account rather than an Administrator.

concepts.name: User state migration tool (USMT)
concepts.explanation: A command-line utility used by IT pros to capture and seamlessly transfer user files, settings, and profiles during a Windows OS upgrade.
concepts.example: Running a script during a hardware replacement cycle to copy a user's local Documents folder and desktop background to their new machine.
concepts.default_value: Standard migration rules capture all local desktop files and user app data configurations unless customized via .xml files.

concepts.name: Autopilot reset
concepts.explanation: A remote or local action that strips away a Windows device's personal data, apps, and settings, returning it to a clean, fully managed state ready for the next user.
concepts.example: A remote worker resigns; the IT team fires an Autopilot Reset to wipe the machine and leave it sitting cleanly at the Windows login screen for a replacement worker.
concepts.default_value: The device preserves its established keyboard, language, and Wi-Fi connection configurations to ensure it remains manageable over the cloud.

concepts.name: DisableAtomaticReDeplymentCredentials Policy
concepts.explanation: A security policy setting that prevents standard users from triggering a local Autopilot Reset via keyboard shortcuts on the sign-in screen.
concepts.example: Blocking regular employees from using the Ctrl + Win + R hotkey shortcut on a login page to wipe their machine.
concepts.default_value: Set to Not Configured, meaning local automatic redeployment capabilities are accessible on the lock screen if local admin credentials are supplied.

concepts.name: Windows Enterprise Multi Session remote Desktops
concepts.explanation: A specialized Windows OS SKU designed exclusively for Azure Virtual Desktop that allows multiple remote users to share a single virtual machine simultaneously.
concepts.example: Provisioning a single powerful cloud VM that simultaneously hosts separate virtual secure desktops for 15 remote call-center workers.
concepts.default_value: Standard user profiles are managed via FSLogix containers to decouple user data from the local operating system drive.

concepts.name: Windows 365 / Cloud PC
concepts.explanation: A cloud-based service that streams a personalized, secure Windows desktop experience directly from Microsoft's cloud to any user device, managed fully within Intune.
concepts.example: Giving a contractor a secure, cloud-hosted Windows 11 desktop that they can log into securely from their personal MacBook.
concepts.default_value: Automatically provisions with automated monthly patch cycles managed by Windows Autopatch.

concepts.name: Enterprise Security Baseline
concepts.explanation: A collection of Microsoft-recommended, pre-configured security settings designed to help administrators quickly apply proven best-practice defenses.
concepts.example: Pushing out the Windows 11 Security Baseline to instantly turn on advanced credential protection and complex local password requirements.
concepts.default_value: Settings align strictly with Microsoft’s official Security Compliance Toolkit recommendations.

concepts.name: Account Protection
concepts.explanation: A dedicated endpoint security policy focused specifically on safeguarding user identity credentials, covering features like Windows Hello for Business and credential guarding.
concepts.example: Enforcing a policy requiring users to set up a biometric Windows Hello Face/PIN instead of traditional passwords.
concepts.default_value: Windows Hello for Business defaults to Enabled globally across basic tenant onboarding.

concepts.name: Microsoft Defender for iOS
concepts.explanation: The mobile security app that protects iPhones and iPads against phishing, unsafe network connections, and malicious web content.
concepts.example: Automatically blocking an iPhone user from loading a malicious link clicked from an SMS text message.
concepts.default_value: Web Protection (Anti-phishing) is enabled by default upon completion of the user's initial app login.

concepts.name: Conditional Access
concepts.explanation: An identity-driven security engine that evaluates real-time signals (like device compliance and location) to enforce access controls before granting entry to corporate apps.
concepts.example: Forcing a user to complete an MFA prompt only if they are logging into corporate apps from an unrecognized country.
concepts.default_value: New tenants deploy with Microsoft Security Defaults enabled, enforcing standard MFA for all users.

concepts.name: Conditional Access Policy
concepts.explanation: The specific, structured rule defined within Microsoft Entra ID that enforces blocks or multifactor authentication based on user compliance and risk criteria.
concepts.example: A rule stating: 'If a user tries to access Exchange Online from a non-compliant laptop, then Block Access entirely.'
concepts.default_value: Policies are created in Report-only mode by default so admins can test the impact before turning them on live.

concepts.name: Protection Policy
concepts.explanation: A general term representing security configurations designed to guard corporate resources, frequently used to refer to application or data layer security templates.
concepts.example: Applying an Endpoint Security policy to ensure local client firewalls are permanently running on all company laptops.
concepts.default_value: Security components act as additive policies that overlay on top of existing baseline configuration profiles.

concepts.name: Types of Compliance Policy
concepts.explanation: The various categories of rules (such as OS version, encryption status, or firewall state) used to determine whether an endpoint is considered healthy and secure.
concepts.example: Setting up individual, distinct compliance policies for Windows 11 compliance vs. iOS compliance.
concepts.default_value: Devices are checked for compliance against native parameters every 8 hours by default.

concepts.name: Compliance Status Validity
concepts.explanation: A setting that defines exactly how many days a device has to report its status before Intune automatically marks it as 'noncompliant' due to inactivity.
concepts.example: Marking a laptop as noncompliant if an employee goes on vacation and leaves the computer powered off in a drawer for more than 30 consecutive days.
concepts.default_value: Set globally to 30 days out of the box.

concepts.name: Compliance assigned as setting
concepts.explanation: A specific rule configured inside a compliance policy that dictates a precise technical standard a device must meet to pass health validation.
concepts.example: Explicitly changing the Require BitLocker setting toggle to Require within your corporate compliance profile.
concepts.default_value: Most settings inside a fresh compliance policy are initially set to Not Configured.

concepts.name: Device Compliance Policy
concepts.explanation: A set of platform-specific security requirements that endpoints must satisfy to be flagged as healthy and permitted to access corporate resources via Conditional Access.
concepts.example: A core company policy requiring all MacBooks to run at least macOS Sonoma and have FileVault disk encryption enabled.
concepts.default_value: 'Mark devices with no assigned compliance policy as' defaults to Compliant (Security best practice is to change this to Noncompliant).

concepts.name: Attack Surface Reduction (ASR)
concepts.explanation: A suite of endpoint security rules that blocks behaviors commonly exploited by malware, such as launching executable files from emails or scripts.
concepts.example: Enforcing a rule that blocks Microsoft Word from spawning executable child processes (preventing malicious macro viruses from executing code).
concepts.default_value: Individual rules are typically set to Not Configured or Audit Mode until explicitly switched to Block.

concepts.name: Endpoint detection and response (EDR)
concepts.explanation: Advanced security policies that integrate Intune with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint to monitor, detect, and automatically remediate malicious activities on endpoints.
concepts.example: Configuring Intune to automatically offboard/isolate a machine from the local network if live ransomware behavior is detected on it.
concepts.default_value: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint client configuration packages are set to automatically renew and stream telemetry to your security center.

concepts.name: Mitigate to Windows LAPS from legacy LAPS
concepts.explanation: The architectural migration of transitioning from old active-directory local administrator password management to the modern, cloud-native Windows Local Administrator Password Solution integrated into Intune.
concepts.example: Decommissioning legacy GPOs that saved local passwords to plain-text Active Directory attributes and enabling the native Intune LAPS endpoint policy instead.
concepts.default_value: The modern cloud version defaults to a password complexity structure requiring Large letters, small letters, numbers, and special characters.

concepts.name: Protect identities in Entra ID
concepts.explanation: Utilizing security features like identity protection, multi-factor authentication, and risk scoring within the cloud directory to prevent credential theft and unauthorized access.
concepts.example: Implementing an identity policy that blocks all user login attempts originating from anonymous proxy networks or Tor browsers.
concepts.default_value: Risky sign-in policies are set to Audit-only until explicit access blocks or MFA remediation controls are turned on.

concepts.name: Jailbreak detection
concepts.explanation: A security capability that scans iOS and Android operating systems for unauthorized root modifications, instantly triggering policy actions to isolate noncompliant devices.
concepts.example: Evaluating file paths like /Applications/Cydia.app on iOS devices during sync to check if the underlying sandbox has been compromised.
concepts.default_value: Handled natively by the Intune Company Portal or Microsoft Authenticator app during its routine security check cycles.

concepts.name: Update Ring
concepts.explanation: A policy that defines how and when Windows Quality and Feature updates are deployed across various groups of devices over designated deferral timeframes.
concepts.example: Configuring an update ring where IT personnel get updates immediately (0-day deferral) while the rest of the company gets them 10 days later.
concepts.default_value: Quality update deferral period defaults to 0 days, and Feature update deferral period defaults to 0 days on a fresh profile.

concepts.name: Feature update policy
concepts.explanation: A configuration that locks Windows devices into a specific version of the operating system (e.g., Windows 11, version 23H2) and prevents upgrades past that point until authorized.
concepts.example: Ensuring your entire corporate fleet stays strictly on Windows 11 23H2 and skips 24H2 until the corporate app team gives approval.
concepts.default_value: Devices will update to the absolute newest version available over the cloud unless a specific version target policy is assigned.

concepts.name: Quality update policy
concepts.explanation: Rules that govern the scheduling, installation, and forced restarts for monthly Windows security and bug-fix updates.
concepts.example: Forcing laptops to automatically download the monthly Microsoft 'Patch Tuesday' security fixes and schedule mandatory installations at 3:00 AM.
concepts.default_value: Automatic update behavior defaults to 'Auto install at maintenance time'.

concepts.name: Ring policy
concepts.explanation: The foundational update deployment structure used to stagger software patches across a gradual rollout schedule (e.g., Pilot, Fast, Slow) to minimize business disruption.
concepts.example: Deploying a patch to 5% of machines on Monday, 25% on Wednesday, and the final 70% on Friday if no issues arise.
concepts.default_value: Restarts are deferred with a deadline of 3 days for quality updates before forcing a device reboot.

concepts.name: Compliance Profile for macOS
concepts.explanation: A targeted set of health rules—such as requiring FileVault encryption or a specific minimum OS version—that Mac computers must satisfy to access corporate apps.
concepts.example: Flagging an employee's MacBook Pro as noncompliant because they turned off system password locks.
concepts.default_value: System integrity protection (SIP) checks default to Required for standard Apple compliance checks.

concepts.name: Device Configuration profile for macOS
concepts.explanation: A customized payload used to push operational settings, such as Wi-Fi profiles, system extensions, and custom preferences, to Mac endpoints.
concepts.example: Pushing a .mobileconfig file that forces the corporate desktop wallpaper onto all enterprise Mac devices.
concepts.default_value: Configured profiles run with Root/System privileges on the local macOS operating system.

concepts.name: Device type restriction for macOS
concepts.explanation: A global enrollment filter used to either block personal Mac computers from registering or restrict Apple enrollment entirely based on ownership type.
concepts.example: Blocking personal employee MacBooks from enrolling via the web portal while allowing corporate MacBooks to onboard via automated systems.
concepts.default_value: Personally owned devices for the macOS platform defaults to Allow.

concepts.name: Software Update policy for macOS
concepts.explanation: A policy that controls the visibility, scheduling, and deferrals of system updates and patches across managed Mac computers.
concepts.example: Setting macOS critical security updates to automatically install within 24 hours of release without waiting for user confirmation.
concepts.default_value: Product updates are set to Default behavior (user receives standard system notifications from Apple).

concepts.name: Endpoint Analytics
concepts.explanation: A cloud analytics service that evaluates device performance, startup times, and software reliability to help IT proactively improve the digital user experience.
concepts.example: Opening the console to discover that 40 laptops are suffering from slow boot times caused by an outdated antivirus driver application.
concepts.default_value: Requires data collection settings to be switched to Enhanced mode inside the Windows telemetry configuration.

concepts.name: Assignment Failure report
concepts.explanation: A troubleshooting dashboard that highlights exactly which policies or applications failed to deploy to specific users or devices, along with error codes.
concepts.example: Reviewing a dashboard to find that a corporate VPN profile failed to install on a laptop due to error code 0x87D101F4 (remediation timeout).
concepts.default_value: Refreshes continuously and retains detailed system deployment error history for 30 days.

concepts.name: Windows feature update device readiness report
concepts.explanation: An analytics report that assesses whether managed devices meet the strict hardware requirements needed to successfully upgrade to a newer version of Windows.
concepts.example: Verifying how many aging company desktop machines lack the necessary TPM 2.0 chips required to upgrade to Windows 11.
concepts.default_value: Categorizes all active endpoints into status groupings: Capable, Not Capable, or Insufficient Data.

concepts.name: Windows feature update device comparability risks report
concepts.explanation: A diagnostic view that pinpoints potential application or driver incompatibilities that might cause a feature update to fail on specific devices.
concepts.example: Seeing a warning that 12 engineering laptops will crash during an update because their current CAD software version isn't supported on the new OS build.
concepts.default_value: Data is derived directly from global Microsoft app telemetry tracking databases.

concepts.name: Device compliance report
concepts.explanation: A high-level administrative dashboard that displays the overall health status of all organization devices, categorizing them as compliant, noncompliant, or not evaluated.
concepts.example: A CISO pulling a quick pie-chart graphic showing that 98% of the organization's mobile fleet is securely compliant with security rules.
concepts.default_value: Filtered automatically to show live Active devices that checked in within the last 30 days.

concepts.name: Intune RBAC and Scope Group
concepts.explanation: A security model that combines Role-Based Access Control to limit what actions an administrator can perform with Scope Tags to restrict which specific devices they can see.
concepts.example: Giving a London IT technician full rights to wipe devices, but only if those devices carry the 'UK-Region' scope tag.
concepts.default_value: The built-in administrator account carries the Default scope tag, giving them unrestricted access to everything.

concepts.name: Intune roles
concepts.explanation: Defined sets of administrative permissions (such as Help Desk Operator or Application Manager) that control access within the Intune admin center.
concepts.example: Assigning a junior technician the Help Desk Operator role so they can trigger device syncs and password resets but cannot delete apps.
concepts.default_value: Intune provides 10+ built-in roles out-of-the-box ready for immediate assignment.

concepts.name: Bulk device actions to delete
concepts.explanation: An administrative operation used to purge multiple selected device records completely out of the Intune management system simultaneously.
concepts.example: Selecting 150 legacy laptops that were decommissioned and sold, then deleting them from the system database in a single action.
concepts.default_value: You can process a maximum limit of 1000 devices in a single bulk action operation.

concepts.name: Bulk device actions to retire
concepts.explanation: A mass-action command that simultaneously removes corporate data, applications, and policies from a selected group of devices while retaining personal user data.
concepts.example: Retiring 40 personal smartphones belonging to a sales team after transitioning them over to newly issued corporate devices.
concepts.default_value: Once triggered, the target devices process the retirement command the next time they complete a background check-in cycle.

concepts.name: Rotate Bitlocker keys remote action
concepts.explanation: A security command sent over the cloud that forces a Windows endpoint to instantly generate a brand-new BitLocker recovery key and upload it back to Entra ID.
concepts.example: Forcing a new key generation because a technician accidentally looked at and copied a user's original BitLocker recovery key during a support ticket.
concepts.default_value: Requires the client machine to be actively running Windows 10/11 Azure AD Joined with local administrative access available to the OS.

concepts.name: Device Delete, Retire, Sync, Wipe
concepts.explanation: The core suite of remote actions used to completely remove a record (Delete), strip company data (Retire), force a policy check-in (Sync), or factory reset a machine (Wipe).
concepts.example: Sending a remote Wipe command to an executive's laptop that was stolen from an airport terminal to erase all data on the hard drive.
concepts.default_value: The Sync command will attempt to ping the device up to 3 times consecutively before timing out over the web.

concepts.name: Which devices can activated by using subscription activation
concepts.explanation: Windows Pro devices owned by users assigned a Windows Enterprise E3 or E5 license can automatically upgrade to Windows Enterprise without a reboot or product key.
concepts.example: A user logs into a retail-bought Windows 11 Pro laptop with their corporate E5 account, instantly transforming the OS into Windows 11 Enterprise.
concepts.default_value: This background upgrade process executes silently without requiring any system restarts or entering a 25-digit product license key.

concepts.name: Device cleanup rules
concepts.explanation: Automated administrative criteria that automatically delete inactive, stale, or unresponsive device records from Intune after a set number of days.
concepts.example: Automatically deleting any device record from your console if the machine hasn't connected or pinged the service in over 90 days.
concepts.default_value: Out-of-the-box cleanup rules are turned Off (when enabled, the standard recommended default value is 90 days).

concepts.name: Remote Bitlocker keys rotation
concepts.explanation: An on-demand security feature that allows an IT administrator to change a device's encryption recovery key remotely via the cloud console.
concepts.example: Clicking the 'BitLocker key rotation' button inside a specific device's Intune page after a security breach incident.
concepts.default_value: Successfully rotated keys are instantly backed up to Microsoft Entra ID before the old key is systematically deprecated on the client.

concepts.name: Device Query
concepts.explanation: An advanced feature that allows administrators to use Kusto Query Language (KQL) to request real-time configuration and operational data directly from an active Windows device.
concepts.example: Running the live query `Registry('HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\MyCustomApp')` to verify if a specific system registry patch is present on a user's machine right now.
concepts.default_value: Queries run live against the endpoint and automatically time out if the target machine fails to respond within 2 minutes.

concepts.name: Remote Device Actions
concepts.explanation: The broad collective term for cloud-initiated commands—such as restart, lock, sync, or wipe—sent instantly from the Intune console to an endpoint.
concepts.example: Initiating a remote Remote Lock on an employee's iPad because they left it exposed on a table at a public coffee shop.
concepts.default_value: Commands are wrapped in secure Apple APNs or Windows WNS notification packets for near-instant push execution.

concepts.name: Device authentication
concepts.explanation: The secure validation process used to verify a device's identity via certificates, TPM chips, or tokens before allowing it to communicate with management services or access resources.
concepts.example: Enforcing a rule where an Android phone must present a valid, Intune-issued SCEP certificate before it is allowed to connect to corporate Wi-Fi networks.
concepts.default_value: Utilizes industry-standard OAuth 2.0 token validation structures during standard registration check-ins.

concepts.name: Device Sync
concepts.explanation: A command that forces an endpoint to immediately check in with Intune to download the latest available apps, policies, and configuration updates.
concepts.example: Pushing out an urgent security update and sending a manual 'Sync' command from the web console to force an employee's machine to download it immediately instead of waiting 8 hours.
concepts.default_value: Laptops automatically execute an internal background sync task every 8 hours if no manual command is sent.

concepts.name: Remote Help in intune
concepts.explanation: A secure, cloud-based help desk tool integrated directly into Intune that allows IT technicians to remotely view and control a user's screen during troubleshooting sessions.
concepts.example: A support agent generating a 6-digit session code to securely take control of a remote worker's desktop to fix a broken printing driver.
concepts.default_value: Unattended access capability defaults to Disabled to ensure end-user privacy consent is always required before screen sharing.

concepts.name: Microsoft Cloud PKI
concepts.explanation: A cloud-native Public Key Infrastructure service that allows IT to easily generate, issue, and manage security certificates directly within Intune without on-premises servers.
concepts.example: Issuing secure device authentication certificates to 5,000 corporate laptops to authorize automatic VPN access without deploying local active directory certificate services.
concepts.default_value: Root certification authority validity periods are automatically set to 25 years by default upon initialization.

concepts.name: Exclusion vs. Inclusion Groups
concepts.explanation: Inclusion groups explicitly target a policy to specific sets of users or devices, whereas Exclusion groups act as an overriding veto to ensure certain members never receive that specific policy.
concepts.example: Deploying a restrictive wallpaper policy to an inclusion group named 'All-Staff', while simultaneously adding the 'Executive-Team' to the exclusion group so they can keep their personal backgrounds.
concepts.default_value: Intune calculation logic prioritizes Exclusions over Inclusions in all scenarios where a user belongs to both targeted groups.

concepts.name: Wipe vs. Retire
concepts.explanation: A Wipe executes a full factory reset to clear all personal and corporate data from a device, whereas a Retire selectively deletes only corporate data, keeping personal files untouched.
concepts.example: Choosing Wipe for a lost corporate phone to erase everything, but using Retire for a personal BYOD phone when an employee departs the company.
concepts.default_value: If a device is encrypted via BitLocker, a Wipe action will securely discard the local encryption keys to render the hard drive completely unreadable.

concepts.name: Co-Management & Tenant Attach
concepts.explanation: Co-Management allows a Windows device to be simultaneously managed by both on-premises Configuration Manager and cloud Intune, while Tenant Attach syncs Configuration Manager devices directly to the cloud admin console for instant remote actions.
concepts.example: Moving the 'Compliance Policies' workload slider to Intune to manage device health via the cloud while keeping 'App Deployment' running through your on-premises SCCM infrastructure.
concepts.default_value: The capability matrix uses Workload Sliders that point explicitly to either Configuration Manager or Intune as the authoritative owner for specific feature buckets.

concepts.name: Intune Suite / Advanced Add-ons
concepts.explanation: A premium collection of advanced endpoint management capabilities—such as Cloud PKI, Remote Help, and Endpoint Privilege Management—available as specialized licenses on top of standard Intune.
concepts.example: Purchasing the add-on suite to implement Endpoint Privilege Management so standard users can temporarily elevate their privileges to install specific approved developer utilities.
concepts.default_value: Individual advanced add-on modules are turned Off and hidden in the console until active subscription add-on licenses are added to the tenant billing portal.

concepts.name: Microsoft tunnel gateway, for mobile
concepts.explanation: A Linux-based VPN gateway solution that allows iOS and Android devices to securely access on-premises corporate networks and resources using modern authentication.
concepts.example: Setting up an on-demand secure pipeline so that whenever an iPhone user opens an internal intranet application, it securely connects via the Tunnel architecture without user interaction.
concepts.default_value: Requires separate Linux host VM configurations using Docker containers running on-premises or within a cloud infrastructure pool.
